title: Thin-margin activation scratchbook
content:
(personal scratchbook) — aiming to be quick, noisy, and actionable

Goal: sketch a tiny product-tier and activation subsidy that drives 2–3x trial->paid conversion for small apps, while keeping long-run unit margin >= 15% on hosted.

Assumptions / back-of-envelope constants (plausible):
- GPU amortization: $6.5 / GPU-hour effective for small hosted pool (after infra + support).
- Throughput: 250k tokens / GPU-hour (mixed short/medium prompts, some batching) -> $6.5 / 250k = $0.000026 / token (infrastructure only)
- Additional infra + infra engineering ops overhead: +30% -> $0.000034 / token
- Storage / embeddings / metadata + api infra: +$0.000006 / token
- Total variable cost (baseline): ~ $0.00004 / token (~$40 / million tokens)
- Non-token costs (calls, sessions): amortized auth + telemetry: $0.001 per session on average (ballpark)

Quick margin math: if we charge $0.00008 / token (8c per 1k tokens) -> gross margin per token = 0.00004 -> 50% on tokens alone. But... need to account for discounting, burst capacity, customer support, SLOs. Target net margin target: 15–25% overall.

Activation subsidy design idea (microcommit model):
- Offer a "starter pack": 250k tokens + 1000 inference calls (session lighting) for $5 first-month credit (pays for infra + small activation subsidy).
- Backcalc: 250k tokens cost ~ $10 (at 0.00004) -> so $10 cost vs $5 price = -$5 subsidy (we buy trial). But conversion signal is strong for customers that use >100k tokens in trial. Need to cap subsidy.
- Alternative: structure as "pay $5, get 250k tokens but per-token billing after 50k at normal rates" — throttles unbounded consumption.

Per-session framing (helps conversational apps):
- Define a session = sequence of requests with same convo id over 30 minutes. Typical session token usage distribution: median 600 tokens, mean 3k (heavy tail).
- If target is SMB chatbots, a starter of 200 sessions + 50k tokens for $5 looks attractive.
- Cost to us: sessions cost ~200 * 0.001 = $0.2; tokens cost = $2 -> $2.2 cost vs $5 revenue -> small positive. Good trade if conversion follows.

Edge controls to limit runaway subsidies:
- Include per-session soft cap and rate limit (after N tokens/session reduce sampling temperature or downgrade model to quantized variant automatically).
- Require card on file to claim starter pack; prevents abuse.
- Limit to one starter per org/email domain (harder to enforce but worth).

Token math notes (batching + KV cache effect):
- For retrieval-augmented flows, effective tokens generated per model invocation is smaller but context length increases. Cache hit reduces per-token compute cost by ~20–60% depending on prefix reuse.
- If average cache hit = 30% then effective variable token cost = base_token_cost * (1 - 0.3 * cache_speedup_factor). Need more data.

Model variance and fallback policy:
- Host two model tiers: standard (higher quality, higher cost) and economy (quantized, cheaper). Pricing differential should reflect cost ratio. If economy is 60% of price, then cost ratio likely ~0.5; margin dynamics allow offering economy for baseline tiers.

Tier proposal (simple):
- Free / dev tier: 2k tokens / 20 requests / limited throughput (0 margin, purely activation). Cardless, very limited.
- Starter ($5): 50k tokens + 200 sessions; conditional (card), limited to 30 days. Goal: LTV signal.
- Pay-as-you-go: $0.00008 per token (hosted standard) with 30-day usage reaction alert.
- Committed mini (monthly $200): 3M tokens + guaranteed throughput burst; effective per-token price = $0.000066 -> commit discount vs PAYG.
- Dedicated entry (for teams): reserve 1 GPU-equivalent for $X/month -> more complex calc.

Quick scenario (churn sensitivity):
- Acquisition cohort: 1000 trial signups. Conversion assumptions: cardless free -> 3% convert, starter with card -> 12% convert. If we push more users to Starter (card required) conversion lifts but signup friction rises. Which balances better? Run quick LTV calc.
- Expected revenue per converting customer in first 6 months: assume avg usage month 1 = 500k tokens, month2-6 decay 40% month-over-month -> total tokens ~1.1M -> revenue @ $0.00008 = $88; cost @ $0.00004 = $44 -> gross margin $44 -> cover CAC if CAC <$44.

CAC levers: free vs paid-first access. If requiring card for starter increases CAC by 20% but doubles conversion multiplier (to 24% effective), it's worth it if CAC still < LTV. Need A/B.

Open questions / data to pull:
- Real amortized tokens per GPU-hour on prod (date range last 3 months). Current estimate is noisy. Pull metrics: tokens_per_gpu_hour_by_model (gpt-like, opt variants).
- Real median tokens per session across product categories (chat, completion, embedding+retrieval).
- Cache hit distribution and savings.
- Historical conversion delta when card is required vs optional.

Immediate TODOs (experiments):
- A: Launch Starter ($5) as described, card required, 30-day; track activation->paid 90-day conversion.
- B: Cardless free flow with 2k tokens vs Starter; compare CAC and downstream usage quality (if they hit >50k tokens do we get ledger? send nudge).
- Track cohorts by model used (economy vs standard) to measure real per-token cost.

Small heuristics to remember:
- Users rarely convert purely on token price; reliability, throughput, and integrated features (audit logs, SSO) are often bigger signals for enterprise. For SMB, activation velocity matters.
- Give small wins (prebaked templates, starter datasets) that cause >25% uplift in average session length during trial -> raises immediate engagement and perceived value.

Random brain dump / heuristics:
- If median token usage / active user is <10k, price-per-user subscription makes sense (simple buckets), but if >100k per month, commit bands are better.
- Very narrow margin operations: prioritize caching + batch improvements before price increases. 10% caching improvement => direct margin boost.

Notes to self: this is messy. Pull real infra cost numbers before committing to starter pricing. Plan one quick A/B and instrument hard.

End of scratchbook.
